def-controlled-and-natural-mediation-eff:
## Definition

Fix a target population, two treatment versions $a,a'$, a mediator random
element $M$ in a standard-Borel space [[def-standard-borel-space]], and a real random variable $Y$ [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]. Let $M(a)$ be
the mediator response under $do(A=a)$ and let $Y(a,m)$ be the outcome response
under the joint intervention $do(A=a,M=m)$, with the intervention semantics of
[[def-recursive-structural-causal-model-and-dag]]. These are full-data random
variables; consistency alone does not identify their joint law from observed
data.

When the displayed differences are integrable [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]], the **controlled direct
effect** at mediator setting $m$ is
$$\operatorname{CDE}_m(a,a')=E[Y(a,m)-Y(a',m)].$$
It requires that setting the mediator to $m$ be a meaningful intervention.
The **natural direct effect** and **natural indirect effect**, with $a'$ the
reference treatment level, are
$$\operatorname{NDE}(a,a')=E[Y(a,M(a'))-Y(a',M(a'))],$$
$$\operatorname{NIE}(a,a')=E[Y(a,M(a))-Y(a,M(a'))].$$
The first argument is the active outcome treatment level and the second is the
reference level that supplies the mediator response. When $a\ne a'$, these
targets involve nested counterfactuals from different intervention regimes.
They are defined on a full-data law whether or not they are identified by the
observed law. The total mean contrast is
$$\tau(a,a')=E[Y^a-Y^{a'}],$$
using the treatment-only potential outcomes of
[[def-potential-outcomes-and-consistency]]. For $a=1,a'=0$, this agrees with
the ATE convention in [[def-causal-average-treatment-effects]].
def-simple-markovian-mediation-scm:
## Definition

Let $L$ be an observed baseline random element in a standard-Borel space [[def-standard-borel-space]],
$A$ a treatment random element [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]] taking values in a nonempty countable set [[def-countable]] equipped with the discrete sigma-algebra (the full power set), following the treatment-version convention of [[def-potential-outcomes-and-consistency]]. Let $M$ be an observed mediator random element in a standard-Borel space [[def-standard-borel-space]], and let $Y$ be an observed real random variable [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]. A **simple Markovian mediation SCM** is a
recursive structural causal model in the sense of
[[def-recursive-structural-causal-model-and-dag]] whose endogenous variables
are exactly $(L,A,M,Y)$ and whose equations have the form
$$L=f_L(U_L),\qquad A=f_A(L,U_A),\qquad M=f_M(A,L,U_M),\qquad Y=f_Y(A,M,L,U_Y).$$
The functions are jointly measurable in the sense of [[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]], and the exogenous random elements
$U_L,U_A,U_M,U_Y$ are mutually independent [[def-independent-random-elements]], as required by the Markovian
condition in that SCM definition. The graph therefore has no latent common
cause outside $L$ and no additional post-treatment variable that causes both
$M$ and $Y$. This model is a special case of an NPSEM-IE (a nonparametric
structural equation model with independent errors); it is a substantive model
restriction, not a consequence of the observed distribution. It is a
single-unit model; if units interfere, the treatment version must include the
relevant joint assignment or exposure, as required by
[[def-potential-outcomes-and-consistency]].

The mediator and outcome responses are the recursive responses under the
interventions from [[def-controlled-and-natural-mediation-effects]]:
$$M(a)=f_M(a,L,U_M),\qquad Y(a,m)=f_Y(a,m,L,U_Y).$$
In particular, recursion gives $Y^a=Y(a,M(a))$. The model's absence of an
additional post-treatment common cause is part of the hypothesis; if such a
variable is present, this definition does not cover that causal system.
def-interventionist-mediation-effect:
## Definition

Suppose an expanded structural causal model decomposes a treatment into two
substantively meaningful components $N$ and $O$ that can in principle be set
separately. Write $M(n,o)$ and $Y(n,o)$ for the mediator and outcome under
$do(N=n,O=o)$, and $Y(n,o,m)$ for the outcome under the additional
intervention $do(M=m)$, using the intervention semantics of
[[def-recursive-structural-causal-model-and-dag]]. Here $Y(n,o)$ leaves the
mediator equation active. Mixed component values must correspond to meaningful
intervention protocols; an arbitrary mathematical relabeling of $A$ is not a
component decomposition. For reference component levels $n,n',o,o'$, the
**separable component contrasts** are
$$\operatorname{SE}_N(n,n';o)=E[Y(n,o)-Y(n',o)],$$
$$\operatorname{SE}_O(o,o';n)=E[Y(n,o)-Y(n,o')],$$
whenever the contrasts are integrable [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]. They refer to feasible component
interventions, not to the nested individual mediator value $M(a')$ in a natural
effect.

For the simple single-mediator structural system, the relevant
**dismissible-component restrictions** are the structural exclusions
$$M(n,o)=M(n),\qquad Y(n,o,m)=Y(n',o,m)\quad\text{for all }n,n',o,m.$$
The first says that the outcome-only component $O$ has no effect on the
mediator. The second says that the mediator-only component $N$ has no direct
effect on the outcome when the mediator is fixed. In other causal systems the
formal dismissible-component conditions are model-specific. Meaningful
component interventions, consistency, positivity, and appropriate
exchangeability conditions are required before these contrasts can be
identified. No identification theorem for separable effects is asserted here;
they define a different target from the natural direct and indirect effects in
[[def-controlled-and-natural-mediation-effects]].
lem-npsem-ie-implies-cross-world-indepen:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice for the conditional-expectation conventions. In a
simple Markovian mediation SCM, for every supplied treatment levels $a,a'$ and
mediator value $m$,
$$M(a')\perp\!\!\!\perp Y(a,m)\mid\sigma(L),$$
$$A\perp\!\!\!\perp M(a')\mid\sigma(L),\qquad A\perp\!\!\!\perp Y(a,m)\mid\sigma(L).$$
Thus independent structural errors supply the cross-world restriction needed
by the natural-effect formula, in addition to the single-world
treatment-outcome, treatment-mediator, and mediator-outcome independences.
def-natural-effect-identification-assump:
## Definition

Fix a pair of treatment levels $a,a'$ in the simple Markovian mediation model
of [[def-simple-markovian-mediation-scm]]. The assumptions used for the
natural-effect formula are:

1. **Consistency and treatment versions.** The treatment versions and joint
   treatment/mediator interventions have the meanings fixed by
   [[def-controlled-and-natural-mediation-effects]]. The observed responses
   satisfy $M=M(A)$ and $Y=Y(A,M(A))$ by the structural recursion.

2. **No unmeasured treatment confounding.** Conditional on baseline $L$, the
   assignment error $U_A$ is independent of the mediator and outcome response
   errors. Equivalently in this model, for every supplied $b,c,m$,
   $A\perp\!\!\!\perp M(b)\mid\sigma(L)$ and
   $A\perp\!\!\!\perp Y(c,m)\mid\sigma(L)$.

3. **No unmeasured mediator–outcome confounding.** Conditional on $L$, the
   mediator and outcome response errors are independent. This excludes an
   unmeasured common cause of $M$ and $Y$ in the stated graph.

4. **No treatment-induced mediator–outcome confounder.** There is no
   post-treatment endogenous variable other than $M$ that is a common cause
   of $M$ and $Y$. If such a variable is present, the four-equation model
   above does not apply.

5. **Cross-world restriction.** For all supplied $b,c,m$,
   $M(b)\perp\!\!\!\perp Y(c,m)\mid\sigma(L)$. In particular this includes
   $M(a')\perp\!\!\!\perp Y(a,m)\mid\sigma(L)$ for the nested response in
   the natural direct effect. The lemma
   [[lem-npsem-ie-implies-cross-world-independence-for-mediation]] proves
   this restriction for the simple NPSEM-IE model. The same-world instances
   $b=c$ express mediator–outcome exchangeability; the instances $b\ne c$
   are additional cross-world assumptions.

6. **Treatment positivity.** $P(A=b)>0$ and
   $P(A=b\mid\sigma(L))>0$ almost surely for each treatment level $b$ used
   in the contrast, in the target-support convention of
   [[def-positivity-for-discrete-treatment]].

7. **Mediator positivity.** Let $Q_b(l,\cdot)$ be a conditional law of $M$
   given $(A,L)=(b,l)$, in the sense of
   [[def-conditional-law-given-a-random-element]]. For the cross-treatment
   response $Y(a,M(a'))$, require
   $$Q_{a'}(l,\cdot)\ll Q_a(l,\cdot)$$
   for almost every $l$ under the law $P_L$ of $L$ from
   [[def-law-or-distribution-of-a-random-element]]. This support-domination
   condition ensures that
   the conditional outcome law observed at treatment $a$ is defined at
   mediator values drawn under treatment $a'$. It is a measure-level
   condition; for a countable mediator it says every $m$ with
   $Q_{a'}(l,\{m\})>0$ also has $Q_a(l,\{m\})>0$.

8. **Integrability.** Every nested outcome $Y(b,M(c))$ used in the displayed
   effects is integrable [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]] under the target population law.

These are sufficient full-data assumptions for the theorem on this page, not
empirical facts certified by a regression fit. The NPSEM-IE independent-error
restriction supplies the cross-world condition. FFRCISTG means “Finest Fully
Randomized Causally Interpretable Structured Tree Graph”; in the single-world
convention described by Hernán–Robins, Chapter 23, its regime-specific laws do
not impose a joint independence between counterfactuals from incompatible
regimes. Thus FFRCISTG alone does not supply the cross-world condition above.
This item uses that source distinction only to name the missing assumption;
the explicit two-law counterexample is a separate B-page result. Standardizing
or fitting a regression does not by itself establish the assumptions above.
thm-natural-effect-identification-under-:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $A$ be the countable-discrete treatment random element in
[[def-simple-markovian-mediation-scm]], let $L$ and $M$ be standard-Borel
random elements [[def-standard-borel-space]] [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]], and let $Y$ be real-valued and integrable
[[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]. Suppose the
full-data law is a simple Markovian mediation SCM from
[[def-simple-markovian-mediation-scm]], with consistency, treatment positivity,
mediator positivity, and the integrability conditions of
[[def-natural-effect-identification-assumptions]]. Fix treatment levels
$a,a'$. Let $Q_b(l,dm)$ be a conditional law [[def-conditional-law-given-a-random-element]] of $M$ given $(A,L)=(b,l)$, and
let $R((b,l,m),dy)$ be a conditional law [[def-conditional-law-given-a-random-element]] of $Y$ given $(A,L,M)=(b,l,m)$.
Define the zero-filled conditional mean
$$\mu_b(l,m)=\begin{cases}\int y\,R((b,l,m),dy),&\int |y|R((b,l,m),dy)<\infty,\\0,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$
Then the nested mean
$$\theta(a,a')=E[Y(a,M(a'))]$$
is the following functional of the observed-data law:
$$\theta(a,a')=\int_{\mathcal L}\int_{\mathcal M}\mu_a(l,m)\,Q_{a'}(l,dm)\,P_L(dl),$$
where $P_L$ is the target-population law [[def-law-or-distribution-of-a-random-element]] of $L$. The support-domination
hypothesis $Q_{a'}(l,\cdot)\ll Q_a(l,\cdot)$ makes the integral independent
of the chosen conditional-mean version. Consequently,
$$\operatorname{NDE}(a,a')=\theta(a,a')-\theta(a',a'),\qquad \operatorname{NIE}(a,a')=\theta(a,a)-\theta(a,a')$$
are identified [[def-identifiability-of-an-estimand]] in this model. The total mean contrast satisfies
$$\tau(a,a')=\operatorname{NDE}(a,a')+\operatorname{NIE}(a,a').$$
The formula is a population identification result; a regression coefficient
alone does not identify these effects.
